_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Lime Tree
suggestions.reason: Chef-patron Patrick Hannity's own room on Lapwing Lane since 1987 — the menu turns over weekly, but the crispy duck stays by popular demand, and nobody's ever accused it of being stuffy.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the restaurant's own coverage on thegoodfoodguide.co.uk, confidentials.com and squaremeal.co.uk: The Lime Tree, 8 Lapwing Lane, West Didsbury M20 2WS, family-run modern British since 1987, chef-patron Patrick Hannity, no evidence of any second site — single-site, high confidence. Didsbury currently has zero venues in docs/data/venues.json despite being a real district since 2026-09-07 (see districts.json's own note); this is one of four candidates researched today specifically to close that gap. Coordinates are street-level (Lapwing Lane/Burton Road junction, West Didsbury) rather than per-building GPS, consistent with this file's existing precision bar — exact geocoding tools were unreachable this run.

suggestions.name: Volta
suggestions.reason: The Unabombers' Burton Road room — globally-inspired small plates and a Sunday roast worth planning round, dog-friendly and rarely in a hurry to turn the table.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via voltafoodanddrink.co.uk, manchestersfinest.com, camra.org.uk and tasteofmanchester.com: Volta, 167 Burton Road, West Didsbury M20 2LN, founded by Luke Cowdrey and Justin Crawford ('The Unabombers'). Chain check: sister venues are Electrik (Chorlton, cocktail/craft-beer bar) and Refuge (Deansgate, already a real venue in docs/data/venues.json) — three venues total, all within Manchester, distinct concepts under one small hospitality group, not a replicated brand. Same precedent already accepted in venues.json for Orka Koncepts (4 Manchester-only venues, confirmed non-chain). Moderate-high confidence — dog-friendly per manchestersfinest.com.

suggestions.name: Saison
suggestions.reason: David Bell's beer-first successor to the old Violet Hour on Burton Road — a serious keg and cask list, small plates built to match it, cocktails for whoever didn't come for the beer.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via saisonbar.co.uk, tasteofmanchester.com and whatpub.com: Saison, 236 Burton Road, West Didsbury M20 2LW, opened in the former Violet Hour unit (that name/site is now closed under the old branding — do not suggest 'The Violet Hour' separately, it no longer trades under that name). Owner David Bell was previously behind Dulcimer (Chorlton) and The Deaf Institute (Northern Quarter) — a small, distinct-concept, Manchester-only group, same precedent as Volta/Electrik/Refuge above and Orka Koncepts already in venues.json. Independently owned per its own site. Moderate confidence.

suggestions.name: Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden
suggestions.reason: Ninety acres gifted to the city in 1915, rockery and alpine beds still doing their job long after the council funding that once made it official — ten minutes from the village and a different pace entirely.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Wikipedia (Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden, coordinates 53.40833/-2.23056 used directly, one of the few this run with exact rather than street-level coordinates), visitmanchester.com and parksandgardens.org: a public park gifted to Manchester by Alderman Fletcher Moss in 1915/1919, between the Mersey and Stenner Woods — council-owned, free entry, not a commercial venue so no chain risk whatsoever. Introduces a new type, 'BOTANICAL GARDEN' — maps onto the existing 'Parks & green space' Do tile's 'Botanical gardens' sub-preference, which previously had no matching venue anywhere in the app (The Carrs in Wilmslow is 'RIVERSIDE PARK', not botanical). High confidence — a real, long-standing, free public park, closes Didsbury's zero Do-category gap.

suggestions.name: The Jane Eyre Chorlton
suggestions.reason: Ancoats' cocktail room did well enough to earn a second, bigger kitchen on Beech Road — the same curated list, more room for families at Sunday roast, and mahogany that doesn't feel bolted on for the occasion.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestersfinest.com, tasteofmanchester.com, manchesterwire.co.uk and designmynight.com: The Jane Eyre Chorlton, 60 Beech Road, Chorlton-cum-Hardy M21 9EG, opened December 2022/early 2023 as the second site of the Ancoats original — The Jane Eyre (Ancoats) is already a real venue in docs/data/venues.json, so this is the same 2-site sibling precedent as Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello, just the reverse direction (Ancoats original, Chorlton second site). High confidence — well-covered by name, no closure signals, distinct menu/room from the Ancoats site per the coverage.

suggestions.name: Casa de Moor
suggestions.reason: Mediterranean small plates and a cocktail list on Beech Road, sibling only to its Heaton Moor original a few miles down the line — a two-site honesty this street tends to reward.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via chorlton.casademoor.com (operator's own site) and Tripadvisor: Casa de Moor, 133 Beech Road, Chorlton M21. Chain check: one sibling site in Heaton Moor, Stockport (casademoor.com) — both within Greater Manchester, small 2-site group, same precedent as the Cibo/Suburban Green/Heddy's family already accepted in venues.json. Introduces a new type, 'MEDITERRANEAN RESTAURANT', left category-only (Eat) since no existing tile fits precisely — same treatment as INDIAN RESTAURANT/JAPANESE RESTAURANT elsewhere in this file. Moderate confidence — real, currently trading, no closure signals found.

suggestions.name: Henry's Cafe
suggestions.reason: Natalie's own café in the old Post Office on The Village — homemade cakes, a dog under every second table, and nobody minding if breakfast runs into afternoon tea.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Companies House (Henry's Cafe (Prestbury) Limited, incorporated 2020), henryscafe.co.uk (operator's own site) and Tripadvisor: Henry's Cafe, The Old Post Office, The Village, Prestbury SK10 4DG, owner-run by Natalie, dog-friendly, single site with no evidence of any other location. Prestbury has 6 venues in docs/data/venues.json (per today's tally), still under the standing 10-venue target — this closes some of that gap even though it lands in Eat (already Prestbury's least-thin category) rather than Do (its actual thinnest), since a good-faith search today didn't turn up a verifiable new Do candidate beyond what the 2026-09-04 bolster pass already found and rejected. High confidence — small, family-run, single-site.

suggestions.name: Knutsford Heritage Centre
suggestions.reason: A reconstructed 17th-century forge on King Street, run entirely by volunteers — the Millennium Tapestry runs thirteen metres round two galleries, and admission is whatever you feel like leaving in the box.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via knutsfordheritage.co.uk (operator's own site), knutsfordtowncouncil.gov.uk and whichmuseum.co.uk: Knutsford Heritage Centre, King Street, Knutsford, a volunteer-run charity in a reconstructed 17th-century timber-framed forge building, free admission (donations welcomed), home of the Knutsford Millennium Tapestry. Not a commercial operation — zero chain risk. Introduces a new type, 'HERITAGE CENTRE', left category-only (Do) since no existing tile fits precisely, though it's closest in spirit to the 'Culture' tile's 'History' sub-preference. High confidence — closes Knutsford's real Do-category gap (previously only 2 Do venues: Oil Art Advisory Gallery, Knutcraft).

suggestions.name: Altrincham Little Theatre
suggestions.reason: A hundred and thirty seats and a drama society older than the building it's in — amateur only in the sense that nobody's paid, not in the sense that anyone's amateur.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via creativetourist.com, clubtheatre.org.uk (operator's own site) and wherecanwego.com: Altrincham Little Theatre, 17 Oxford Road, Altrincham WA14 2ED, a volunteer-run registered charity and drama society tracing back to 1896, 130-seat house, occasional film screenings too. Not a commercial chain of any kind — zero chain risk. High confidence — closes some of Altrincham's real Do-category gap (previously Everyman Cinema, Altrincham Market, Inch Arts).

suggestions.name: Festival Hall
suggestions.reason: The parish's own 1927 assembly rooms, licensed bar included — comedy nights and orchestral programmes sharing a stage built for a music festival that's still running, just under a different name now.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via aefestivalhall.com (operator's own site) and alderleyedge-pc.gov.uk: Festival Hall, Talbot Road, Alderley Edge, built 1927 for the Alderley Edge Music Festival, run by/for Alderley Edge Parish Council, refurbished 2015, hosts comedy, orchestral concerts, fashion shows and community classes. Not a commercial chain — parish/community venue, zero chain risk. Alderley Edge sits at 7 real venues plus one already-pending candidate (Fire Station Social Cucina); this closes part of its real Do-category gap (previously The Yard, Manchester Rare Books). High confidence.
